title: Time Value of Money in Finance
overview: Time-value analysis moves cash flows across dates by compounding forward and discounting backward.
example: Work from a small return series, state the assumptions, calculate the measure, and explain what the number leaves out.

modules.title: Discounted Cash Flow Valuation
modules.explanation: Discounted-cash-flow analysis treats value as dated cash flows translated to one point in time. Cash-flow additivity lets separately valued streams be combined, and an implied return is the rate consistent with today's price and the future cash flows.
steps: Draw the cash-flow timeline and choose a valuation date.
Discount each cash flow with a rate and period that match its risk and timing.
Add present values and test whether the answer moves correctly when the rate changes.

formula.label: Present value
formula.interpretation: Discount each dated cash flow at a rate consistent with its timing and risk.
formula.example: At 5%, 105 received in one year has a present value of 100.

formula.label: Cash flow additivity
formula.interpretation: Cash-flow streams with identical state-by-state payoffs must have the same present value; otherwise an arbitrage is possible.
formula.example: A four-year 100 annuity plus a 300 payment in year 3 replicates payments of 100, 100, 400, and 100, so their present values add.
